appearance: Dry night race; early qualifying clips show daylight/twilight and must not set main-race lighting.
terrain_character: Flat urban marina, close fenced asphalt streets, dense mature broadleaf shade and differentiated civic/modern skyline.
distinctive_geometry: Singapore Flyer: large spoked observation wheel on sloping A-frame legs with capsules and low retail base near pit end.
Esplanade: two low rounded durian shells, triangulated lattice ribs and many small pointed sunshades.
National Gallery: separate Old City Hall colonnade and Old Supreme Court dome, pale civic stone with regular arches.
Fullerton: heavy paleclassical riverfront hotel, rows of tall bays, cornice/parapet and recessed upper courtyard.
Marina Bay Sands: three slender paired/curved glazed towers supporting long curved boat-like skypark; distant landmark stays visible beyond narrow OSMcorridor.

sectors.name: Pit straight and T1–3
sectors.observed: Long white pit buildings face a covered red crowd stand, with bright paired floodlights and yellow pit-edge paint. The first complex has close mesh fences, individual red-white kerbs and paved escape lanes. The actual driver-LEFT pit footprint crosses native zero, approximately4769→163m in the corrected frame. The old4896m center label is historical and superseded.
sectors.registration: Approximate sector association from road shape, map and landmarks, not linear playback time. Bounds are authoring intervals, not surveyed corner boundaries.

sectors.name: Republic Boulevard T4–5
sectors.observed: The Republic Boulevard walls and mesh sit close to the asphalt. Palms, broadleaf crowns and pale modern facades appear behind them. Long rows of floodlights continue overhead. Urban road markings and paved verges should remain visible.
sectors.registration: Approximate sector association from road shape, map and landmarks, not linear playback time. Bounds are authoring intervals, not surveyed corner boundaries.

sectors.name: Raffles Boulevard T6–7
sectors.observed: Glass office and hotel facades have repeated window mullions. Large yellow hatched junctions, city lamps and close barriers define Raffles Boulevard. Millenia, Suntec and Marina Square use their mapped positions, with trees breaking up the building walls. Direct 632/634/636 s continues through T7 and the T7–T8 straight, with the temporary Stamford spectators close on driver RIGHT.
sectors.registration: Approximate sector association from road shape, map and landmarks, not linear playback time. Bounds are authoring intervals, not surveyed corner boundaries.

sectors.name: Stamford, Padang and T8–T10
sectors.observed: The Old City Hall colonnade and former Supreme Court give the Padang section its pale civic architecture. A broad lawn and mature tree canopy sit behind close fencing. Low cricket and recreation clubs face them. Kerbs and yellow junction marks remain distinct. Direct 638 s is RIGHT T8; 640–641 s faces toward T9 with the rounded Swissôtel tower ahead/right above the 30 m Raffles City podium.
sectors.registration: Approximate sector association from road shape, map and landmarks, not linear playback time. Bounds are authoring intervals, not surveyed corner boundaries.

sectors.name: Anderson Bridge and Fullerton hairpin
sectors.observed: Anderson Bridge has narrow masonry edges and balustrades. Fullerton and the Waterboat House frame the riverfront turns, with heavy cornices, tall bays and trees. Escape areas remain paved beside these river walls.
sectors.registration: Approximate sector association from road shape, map and landmarks, not linear playback time. Bounds are authoring intervals, not surveyed corner boundaries.

sectors.name: Esplanade Drive and Connaught
sectors.observed: Esplanade Drive and Connaught are broad paved streets beside grandstands and dense trees. The two spiked Esplanade shells sit beyond the route, with tall office towers and distant marina buildings above the floodlights. Asphalt and wall bases must stay readable at night.
sectors.registration: Approximate sector association from road shape, map and landmarks, not linear playback time. Bounds are authoring intervals, not surveyed corner boundaries.
sectors.coverage_note: Direct EsplanadeDrive views afterT13. ActualT14/T15 corner poses remain unmatched; do not use646s asT14.

sectors.name: New waterfront straight and NS Square bypass
sectors.observed: Modern NS Square bypass/waterfront straight, continuous urban fencing and overhead race-light strings.1250.81s directly shows the Singapore Flyer rim/capsule ring ahead above the road; its white capsule points contrast with a dark rim/sky. Preserve the current19-turn layout without the removed old grandstand tunnel sequence.
sectors.registration: Approximate sector association from road shape, map and landmarks, not linear playback time. Bounds are authoring intervals, not surveyed corner boundaries.

sectors.name: Final corners and pit complex
sectors.observed: The Flyer wheel, low retail base, pit entry and terraces frame the final corners. Bright lights, compact red-white kerbs and yellow paved edges lead back to the white pit roof and main stand. Protection should follow the final curves continuously.
sectors.registration: Approximate sector association from road shape, map and landmarks, not linear playback time. Bounds are authoring intervals, not surveyed corner boundaries.

dimensions_policy: OSM XY footprints are registered geographic evidence. Tagged height and levels are retained verbatim; missing/zero heights are unknown. Roof/detail sizes and sparse-vegetation spacing in native authoring are visual estimates pending cockpit comparison.

source_registration.method: Mapped WGS footprints projected with the composed runtime geo scale, then exact nearest-segment projection to the final native road. Original source-frame footprint/station records remain nested as historical evidence.
source_registration.landmark_extent_note: Centroid station can fall on adjacent arm of circuit; use actual ring and terrain, not centroid station alone. Overlapping compound roof footprints must never become solid road obstructions.

elevation_review.status: The native racing-deck profile now follows registered published topography controls. Raw DEM remains for source comparison and scenery terrain.
findings: Retained GLO-90 surface heights are not road levels amid buildings/trees; no city rooftop spikes in road.

replacement_profile.vertical_datum: Relative to the published profile minimum; absolute diagram altitude is not used.
replacement_profile.interpolation: Piecewise monotone cubic Hermite. Interior Fritsch-Carlson harmonic slopes; flat SF seam. No uniform rescaling of the previous DEM.
replacement_profile.method: Read relative heights from the published numerical extremum labels and drawn trace, then register individual official corners to retained native centerline geometry using FIA maps. Intermediate heights are graphical estimates, not measurements.
replacement_profile.registration_notes: The old20.046mCityHallpeak near2408m is inconsistent with the F1diagram5.3mrange. The real profile has a modest bridge hump betweenT13andT14. Old2016T1–15are retained; currentT16–19correspond to oldT20–23. The new bypass between oldT15/T20is interpolated nearly flat, not copied from removed corners.
replacement_profile.supersedes: Coarse GLO-90 road profile remains retained as source evidence, not as the racing deck. No new lidar or survey is claimed.

observed.name: Singapore floodlight recipe
observed.structure: Small race fittings at roughly 7 m intervals along continuous paired cables, supported about every 42 m; separate civic lamps, including taller curved streetlamps along Esplanade Drive. Lower race-light line at Anderson Bridge with gradual cable-height transitions.
observed.confidence: High for continuous cable strings and separate streetlamps; moderate for bridge distinction; low for metric height/spacing estimates. Cable support registrations are authoring estimates.
